title: Fix #8: Scope selectors for multiple comment forms
body:
# Description

Fix multiple-comment-form initialization so every comma-separated selector is scoped to its post container.

Previously only the first selector received the container prefix. For example, `#commentform,.comment-form` became `#post-one #commentform,.comment-form`, leaving `.comment-form` global. Every delegated handler therefore matched later forms, and submitting the second form could run the first post container's update path.

This change scopes each selector component independently, includes comment links in the same scoping, and rebuilds both frontend bundles.

Fixes #8

## Type of PR

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Other (please describe)

### Where is the Bug?

- [x] Comment posting
- [ ] Lazy loading
- [ ] Error messages and Overlay
- [x] JavaScript file
- [ ] Other

# How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Browser tests
- [ ] Performance tests
- [x] Local testing

A two-post browser reproduction loaded the production bundle with duplicate WordPress comment form IDs/classes. Before the fix, submitting post two selected post one's comments/form/respond containers. After the fix, sequential submissions produced requests for posts 1 and 2 and selected their respective scoped containers.

title: Fix translated comment submission messages
body:
# Description

Fix comment-status messages and other plugin strings so they can follow the active WordPress locale.

- Rename bundled PO/MO catalogs to WordPress's `wp-ajaxify-comments-{locale}` convention, correct the Vietnamese locale to `vi`, and normalize the language-directory path.
- Recompile all bundled MO files from their PO sources and keep them as temporary fallbacks until community replacements are available.
- Keep untouched label defaults in canonical English storage, translate them at runtime, and preserve genuinely customized labels.
- Register translations for admin scripts, correct stray JavaScript text domains, and rebuild the affected bundles.
- Regenerate the source POT, add language directory metadata, and update translator guidance.

Fixes #13

## WordPress.org translation audit

The WordPress.org translation project exists and currently contains 500 stable originals. The 18 bundled locales all show 0% approved stable translations, and no language packs have been generated.

Comparing the bundled catalogs with the current 492-entry source POT found 134 exact translated entries plus 450 fuzzy candidates. Issue #17 tracks importing those translations into GlotPress, obtaining locale-editor review, and removing each bundled fallback only after WordPress.org distributes its replacement pack.

## Type of PR

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Other (please describe)

- [ ] Lazy loading
- [x] Error messages and Overlay

- [x] Other: translation catalog discovery and locale-aware saved defaults

Validation performed:

- `npm run build` completed successfully; the unavailable, unused `@sweetalert2/theme-wordpress-admin` package was omitted only from the local install, and the committed manifests remain unchanged.
- PHP syntax checks passed for all changed PHP and generated asset files.
- `msgfmt --check` passed for all 18 bundled PO catalogs (legacy header warnings only).
- Every MO catalog was decompiled and compared successfully with the non-fuzzy translated entries in its PO source.
- All bundled filenames now match the plugin text domain and WordPress locale, including Vietnamese `vi`.
- The five comment-submission status/error message IDs are translated in every bundled catalog.
- POT regeneration produced the same 492 source message IDs.
- Focused option-label checks confirmed canonical storage, runtime translation, historical defaults, and custom-label preservation.
- ESLint still reports 55 pre-existing errors in the touched source files; none are on changed lines.

title: fix: remediate patchable dependency alerts (#77, #76, #67, #66, #64, #33)
body:
## Summary

- Refresh compatible npm dependency versions together in `package-lock.json`, preserving lockfile v2 and the existing React 18 / WordPress component APIs.
- Raise the webpack manifest floor to `^5.111.1` and override only `@wordpress/components`' UUID dependency to `^11.1.1`. UUID 11 retains both CommonJS and ESM exports; this avoids upgrading the WordPress component library solely to fix UUID.
- Keep the existing typescript-estree minimatch override (`9.0.7`). All other minimatch entries resolve to patched `3.1.5`; source-map-js resolves to `1.2.2`; adm-zip is absent.

## Issue disposition

Resolves #77
Resolves #76
Resolves #67
Resolves #66
Resolves #64
Resolves #33

For #57 and #65: **not resolved**. Registry checks confirm the latest braces (`3.0.3`) and sprintf-js (`1.1.3`) releases are still vulnerable and have no patched release. The full npm audit reports 30 findings cascading from these two dependencies. Removing them requires replacing/upgrading their parent tooling, not just refreshing the lockfile. Do not close these issues on merge.

Some linked issues are stale: before this change, the live GitHub alert inventory listed only UUID, three minimatch alerts, braces, and sprintf-js. The new lockfile verifies the desired patched/absent states for the other linked issues too. GitHub alerts must be rechecked after merge; this PR does not claim they have already closed.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `npm audit --omit=dev --json`: zero vulnerabilities. This applies only to npm's dependency classification; it is not a claim that WordPress-externalized dependencies are risk-free at runtime.
- Full `npm audit --json`: 30 findings (15 moderate, 15 high), all rooted in the unpatched braces and sprintf-js advisories; no UUID, minimatch, webpack, source-map-js, or adm-zip findings.
- `npm ci --ignore-scripts --loglevel=error`: passed on Node 22.22.2 / npm 10.9.7.
- `npm run build`: passed (webpack 5.111.1; 21 Sass warnings plus a Babel plugin deprecation). Generated assets were restored after verification; this is a manifest/lockfile-only PR, not a release asset refresh.
- `./node_modules/.bin/grunt --no-color`: passed.
- Existing ESLint configuration resolves successfully with `eslint --print-config src/js/frontend/index.js`; no source lint pass is claimed.
- UUID CommonJS `v4()` / `validate()` smoke check: passed. The installed WordPress component consumers use `v4()` without options.

## Scope and follow-up

No source, UI, linter configuration, test infrastructure, PHP, or release-version changes are intended. Reference patterns: existing npm overrides in `package.json`, webpack scripts in `package.json`, and `Gruntfile.js`'s packaging task. Rollback is reverting the manifest/lockfile commit and running `npm ci --ignore-scripts`.

Remaining paths: braces is pulled in by micromatch (through TypeScript lint tooling and Grunt); sprintf-js is pulled in by WordPress i18n, Grunt's argparse and underscore.string, and prettier-eslint's argparse. Follow-up on #57 / #65 should inspect these parents in `package-lock.json`, preserve the existing ESLint configuration and Grunt packaging behavior, and verify with a clean install, full audit, production build, and packaging. No unpatched package is being silently risk-accepted here.

PR #30 also edits `package.json` to add quality-check scripts; preserve both its script additions and this PR's dependency changes if it needs conflict resolution.

title: GH#79: fix AJAX validation-error response handling
body:
## Summary

Fixes the HTTP-success validation-error path by removing the unused `commentUrl` argument from its debug log. That argument was evaluated before the later `const commentUrl` initialization, preventing the existing error handler from running in the source script, even with debugging disabled.

The extracted-error handling, submitting-guard cleanup, successful-comment path, and server validation policy are unchanged.

Resolves #79

## Files Changed

- `src/js/frontend/wp-ajaxify-comments.js`: remove the premature debug argument.
- `dist/wpac-frontend-js.js` and `dist/wpac-frontend-js.asset.php`: regenerate the combined frontend bundle and version.
- `dist/wpac-frontend-wp-ajaxify-comments.js` and `dist/wpac-frontend-wp-ajaxify-comments.asset.php`: regenerate the standalone frontend bundle and version.

Generated assets come from the existing production webpack build. Unrelated generated output is excluded. No dependencies, server-side validation, repository test infrastructure, fixtures, or CI gates were changed.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High — comment form handler.
- **Verification:** runtime-verified for the changed frontend path.
- **Final pushed head:** `6e1c9a0ad29bd2c3122bffb1ed5aacd24c7789cd`.
- **Runtime-tested revision:** `a2f2645d1ddc366c8be9063585d78c105b56aa4f`. All five delivered source/asset files are byte-identical at the final head, verified with `git diff --exit-code` over those exact paths. Only history finalization and exclusion of automatically generated runtime bookkeeping followed the browser run. Existing lint and syntax checks were repeated on the final head.
- **Environment:** Node 22.22.2, webpack 5.111.1, ESLint 8.57.1, jQuery 3.7.1, Chromium 152, and an existing WordPress 6.8.2 / PHP 8.2 local test site.

### Acceptance matrix

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP 2xx plus `X-WPAC-ERROR: 1`, debug off and on | Satisfied | Six browser cases across the source and both rebuilt bundles displayed the actual WordPress error, `Error: Please type your comment text.`, replacing the loading message. |
| No ReferenceError; loading completes; submitting guard clears | Satisfied | All ten browser flows reached AJAX completion with `WPAC_SUBMITTING` false and no JavaScript exceptions. |
| Corrected comment can subsequently be submitted; ordinary success remains functional | Satisfied | After a validation error, a corrected real WordPress POST succeeded, emitted `wpacAfterPostComment`, displayed the awaiting-moderation success message, and retained one usable comment form. |
| Non-2xx validation failures remain handled | Satisfied | Three HTTP 400 browser cases, one per source/bundle, displayed the same extracted WordPress error and cleared the submitting guard. |
| Existing lint and build pass | Satisfied | Commands below passed; only the five authorized files are included. |

**Coverage limit:** The existing local WordPress site did not have a deployed Ajaxify server plugin. The current source/bundles were loaded into its real comment page using the existing browser tooling. One-shot DevTools response overrides supplied the `X-WPAC-ERROR` header, HTTP 400 status for non-2xx cases, and successful-comment metadata normally supplied by the plugin. WordPress validation/page response bodies and the corrected POST were real. This is frontend-path runtime evidence, not an unmodified end-to-end deployment of the server plugin or a reproduction of the historical support-site redirect.

### Existing checks

- `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`
- `npm run lint:js -- --max-warnings=0`
- `npm run build`
- `node --check src/js/frontend/wp-ajaxify-comments.js`
- `node --check dist/wpac-frontend-js.js`
- `node --check dist/wpac-frontend-wp-ajaxify-comments.js`
- `php -l dist/wpac-frontend-js.asset.php`
- `php -l dist/wpac-frontend-wp-ajaxify-comments.asset.php`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- The existing pre-push hook passed frontend lint on the implementation pushes. Automatically regenerated, untracked runtime bookkeeping caused the hook to skip its final repetition; the explicit frontend lint and source/bundle/manifest syntax checks above were run successfully on the final pushed head instead. That bookkeeping is not in the final PR diff.

The production build exits successfully with existing Sass deprecation warnings in untouched SCSS and a `babel-plugin-lodash` deprecation notice. These are outside this source-only validation fix; their files and dependency declarations are unchanged.

## Review

- Direct diff/scope review: only the premature source argument and the four relevant generated artifacts changed.
- Independent, inference-only source closeout review: no introduced P0/P1 defect found. The reviewer received the source deletion and adjacent callback contracts, not the generated bundles or full-site runtime.
- Reviewed branch evidence digest: `22610bc48894e83c03354f58573fab078a07cba40d22f5d3d4ce15b054021298`.
- Final-head branch evidence digest: `c9475f33b3f131f20bdfa78659a3d99c96a5b3ed7b9b8ef60ccc032af453a1d4`. The source/asset file contents reviewed and runtime-tested above are unchanged.

## Rollback

Revert the scoped source and generated-asset changes together.
